findings.title: Template variables and ad-hoc filters are applied twice on the split paths
findings.description:
`runSplitQuery` now calls `applyTemplateVariables` on every target (querySplitting.ts:299). Its sub-requests go through `datasource.runQuery` (datasource.ts:350-353) into `super.query`, and `DataSourceWithBackend.query` calls `this.applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again for each target (packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185). The sub-requests carry `filters` because they spread the original request, so ad-hoc filters are added twice and variables are substituted twice. Before this change the time-split path substituted once. The sharded path added ad-hoc filters once and now adds them three times (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52, then querySplitting.ts:299 via shardQuerySplitting.ts:163, then DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185).

The effect depends on the filter type. Stream-selector filters are protected by the `labelExists` check in `addFilterToStreamSelector` (modifyQuery.ts:494). Parsed and structured-metadata filters go through `addFilterAsLabelFilter` (modifyQuery.ts:511-541), which has no such check. A query like `… | logfmt | level="info"` therefore reaches the backend as `… | logfmt | level="info" | level="info"`. The repeated predicate is idempotent, so results should not change for typical values. The query text, query inspector output, and cache key do change, and a second substitution pass can re-expand any `$name` text that came from a variable value.

Suggested fix: give each path one interpolation owner. The shard path needs interpolated expressions for grouping and selector injection. The time-split path needs them only for classification. Make the other layers skip their own pass, and add a test that goes through the real `runQuery` / `super.query`.

findings.title: Reordered filter in the sharded path can hang the query on an empty expression
findings.description:
The old code interpolated first and then filtered on `expr` (`interpolateVariablesInQueries(...).filter(expr)`), so a target whose expression was only a template variable resolving to an empty string was dropped. The new order filters first, so that target survives. Tracing the new path:

1. `requestSupportsSharding` is false for an empty expression (queryUtils.ts:319-331), so the target goes into the non-sharded group (shardQuerySplitting.ts:246-249).
2. `interpolateShardingSelector` returns the targets unchanged when there are no shards (queryUtils.ts:392-393).
3. `runSplitQuery` drops it at querySplitting.ts:298, leaving zero requests.
4. `runSplitGroupedQueries` evaluates `requests.filter(...)[0].partition` at querySplitting.ts:96, which throws on an empty array.
5. The throw happens inside `groupTargetsByQueryType(...).then(...)` (shardQuerySplitting.ts:213). The rejection is unhandled and the observable never emits.

The trigger needs `lokiShardSplitting`, which is experimental with no default-on expression (registry.go:151-156). It also needs a request with at least one sharding-eligible target plus a second target that resolves to empty. The empty-group crash predates this change: when every target is dropped, shardQuerySplitting.ts:69 reads `groups[0]` from an empty array.

Suggested fix: restore the old order (`map` before the `expr` filter), and guard against empty `requests` in `runSplitGroupedQueries`.

findings.title: `$__auto` in the sharded path is now resolved per time chunk
findings.description:
Previously `interpolateVariablesInQueries` passed `scopedVars` straight to `templateSrv.replace` (datasource.ts:429-447), so `$__auto` was resolved on the frontend once for the whole request. `applyTemplateVariables` strips `__auto` from `scopedVars` (datasource.ts:1113), so it now stays in the query for the backend. For range queries the backend derives the step from the query's own time range when no step is set (`safeStep = timeRange / 11000`, pkg/tsdb/loki/step.go:27-33, called from parse_query.go:145-147). Time chunks are at most one day (querySplitting.ts:304), so `$__auto` can differ from chunk to chunk.

The time-split path already behaves this way, because `super.query` strips the same variable. This change extends that behavior to shard queries rather than introducing a new mechanism. It is still an unmentioned behavior change with no test. Please confirm it is intended, or keep resolving `$__auto` on the frontend for the shard path.

findings.title: Tests lock in the redundant pass and miss the path where it happens
findings.description:
The assertion changed from one call to `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)`. The five calls are one from `runShardSplitQuery` plus one per sub-request `runSplitQuery`, so the test now treats the redundant interpolation as expected behavior. The two new "Interpolates queries before execution" tests stub `runQuery` (querySplitting.test.ts:83, shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:92), which bypasses `DataSourceWithBackend.query`. Neither can detect the duplicate pass from the first finding. No test passes `filters` through either split path, and none covers the empty-after-interpolation case from the second finding.

Suggested tests: assert the final expression once through the real `runQuery` with a parsed-label ad-hoc filter present; add a template-only expression that resolves to empty; replace the call-count assertion with an assertion on the request that reaches the backend.
